playwright-design.description: Development-only semantic gallery interactions, accessibility and responsive captures; no seeded data.

node-contract.description: Imported connector runtime authorization and safety contracts.

unit.description: One function or a small group, in-process, nothing external.

component.description: A coherent UI component rendered in-process, outer boundaries faked.

architecture-static.description: A codebase, build or dependency rule enforced by reading source or running the compiler. No database.

architecture-db.description: A rule about the live schema, grants or roles, asked of the real local Postgres.

database-integration.description: Domain layer and/or policies against real local Supabase (Auth, Postgres, RLS).

offline-contract.description: A provider or protocol shape checked offline from the web runtime: what an adapter sends a vendor and how it reads the reply, with fetch replaced.

python-unit.description: Python: one function or a small group.

python-component.description: Python: a command or handler with its outer HTTP/database boundary faked.

python-contract.description: Python: a provider or protocol shape, checked offline.

playwright-acceptance.description: Browser journeys against the running app and seeded demo data.

playwright-smoke.description: The smallest deployed-shaped check: app answers, login renders, a session works, the shell loads.

playwright-visual.description: Pixel baselines at desktop/tablet/phone widths for a small set of representative patterns — spacing, alignment and responsive composition, never a business rule. Never in the default run: a baseline drifts with design intent, not with correctness, and a diff here is a prompt to look, not a build failure.

provider-contract.description: A real vendor sandbox, called with credentials. Never in the default run; each test skips itself without its credentials. None exist yet.

apps/web/tests/integration/database/invo.note: Emailing an issued invoice (Work Order 2H) against local PostgreSQL and storage: the message goes from the business's own ready default sender to the email on the invoice customer's own contact record, as a transactional message in Communications, carrying the invoice's recorded PDF in place in finance-documents with its checksum, readable back through Communications as the recorded bytes, with an invoice.emailed event; a member without message.send or invoice.issue, another business and a signed-out caller are refused and see no preview; another contact, another business's customer or any other address is refused, a suppressed address and a customer with no address are explained and nothing is queued; a sender that is no longer verified or a business with no default sender is refused with no fallback address and no message; the send takes no attachment, path, bytes, sender or checksum from the request, Communications cannot attach a finance document by path, and members cannot write attachment rows; an invoice with no PDF, one whose stored bytes no longer match the recorded checksum, or one larger than an email may carry sends nothing; a repeated submission is one message, a second send is refused unless asked for explicitly and then records what it follows, and a key cannot be reused for another invoice; queued, sending, a provider retry, accepted (never called delivered), delivered and failed are reported as the runtime and the delivery webhook record them, with one message throughout; sender and recipient history are unchanged by later contact or sender changes, nobody updates or adds a record and another business reads none; only the preview and the send are executable by members, all definer functions fixed to an empty search path. The send path runs apps/api's invoice-document writer in-process; provider outcomes are recorded through the provider_operator and tenant_email_webhook functions, and nothing is sent to a real provider.

Issued invoice presentation and canonical PDF (Work Order 2G) against local PostgreSQL and storage: Work, direct and proposal invoices each record seller, bill-to, brand and clock in the issuing transaction with no money column; later branding, identity and catalog changes never reach a presentation or a stored PDF; nobody updates, inserts or deletes a presentation and even the owner's update is refused; an invoice issued before presentations is left intact and documented plainly; a retained logo survives replacement and is not readable by a customer or another business; documents and retained logos are stored and recorded only by apps/api's writer (Work Order 2G.1, served in-process): no member, issuer, other business or signed-out caller can store into the private bucket or call a recording, source or builder function, and only the writer and the members' preview and requester functions are executable as granted, all definer functions fixed to an empty search path; the writer acts only for a person with invoice.issue in the invoice's own business, resolving the invoice itself; an object it did not store is never adopted or recorded, even under its own naming; concurrent requests create one PDF, one record, one event and one remaining object, a storage failure can be retried, the writer cannot remove or replace what was recorded, and bytes that differ from the recorded checksum are not served; a retained logo is drawn only when the writer recorded it from the current brand logo with its checksum, a logo changed before issue or one it cannot draw falls back to the business name, and objects placed beside it are ignored; a payment recorded before a retried PDF does not change it, and Work, direct and proposal invoices all get documents; members and the invoice's own customer read the same bytes, while another customer, another business and a signed-out caller read nothing from a private bucket.
